Why This Matters

Authentication continuity is the central issue. Your unengaged subscribers opted in to receive email from your existing sending domain. The DNS records, sender reputation, and authentication signals (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) tied to that domain are the technical trust signals mailbox providers use to decide whether your messages reach the inbox. Sending the same subscribers from a brand-new domain set up for cold outreach breaks that continuity. Even if the recipient is the same person, the sending fingerprint is unrecognizable.

Cold email infrastructure is designed for prospects who never opted in. The 2-4 week warmup period and new domain/mailbox setup exist because cold outreach requires building sender reputation from zero. Applying that machinery to a list that already has reputation history is technically possible but strategically backwards.

Throttled sending from your existing ESP solves the same problem at a fraction of the day-one cost. The risk that re-engagement campaigns pose — spike in complaints, bounces, or unsubscribes damaging your main sender reputation — is real. The solution is controlled volume and segmentation, not parallel infrastructure. A conservative throttle protects your reputation while preserving the authentication trust signals your list already has.

The Instantly approach makes sense for one specific scenario: when your existing ESP reputation is already so damaged that you're better off starting over. If that's the case, the bigger conversation isn't about this one re-engagement campaign.
